# Kspec Automation Session - Task Work

**Session ID:** `01KJQM0DXCNG01HZGX4QJ2BYBG`
**Iteration:** 1 of 30
**Mode:** Automated (no human in the loop)


### Current State

> **Truncated** (105693 bytes). Fetch full data:
> ```
> kspec session start --json
> ```
>
> Summary: `{}`

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

Implement Agent Invocation Lifecycle
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJP277AG4Y6W4WH0SAX7G2W3
Slugs:     implement-agent-invocation-lifecycle
Type:      task
Status:    needs_work
Priority:  3
Automation: eligible
Spec ref:  @agent-invocation-lifecycle
Plan ref:  @plan-reactive-agent-runtime
Depends:
  @implement-agent-definition-schema → Implement Agent Definition Schema [completed]
  @implement-session-model-evolution → Implement Session Model Evolution [completed]

Started:   2026-03-02T14:51:07.443Z

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Invocation Lifecycle
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  Per-invocation session creation, ACP agent spawn, prompt delivery,
  event logging, timeout handling, and structured completion tracking.
  Each dispatch creates an isolated session with its own event log and
  metadata. This is the core building block used by both the dispatch
  engine and CLI one-shot mode.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: An agent is dispatched for a task

    When: The invocation starts

    Then: A new session is created with trigger, agent_id, task_id, and
adapter metadata populated in session.yaml

  [ac-2]
    Given: A session is created for an agent invocation

    When: The ACP agent is spawned

    Then: KSPEC_SESSION_ID is injected into the agent environment using
the existing harness-specific injection (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent invocation is running

    When: The configured timeout_minutes is reached

    Then: The ACP client sends a cancel request, the session is closed
with status timed_out, and a timeout note is added to the task

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent invocation completes successfully

    When: The ACP session ends with stop reason end_turn

    Then: The session is closed with status completed and an
agent.completed event is logged with structured outcome data

  [ac-5]
    Given: An agent invocation fails with a process crash or ACP error

    When: The failure is detected

    Then: The session is closed with status failed, an agent.failed
event is logged with the error details, and the task receives
a failure note

  [ac-6]
    Given: An agent invocation produces streaming output via ACP updates

    When: Session updates arrive from the ACP client

    Then: Events are logged to the session JSONL file with blob
externalization applied to oversized payloads

  [ac-7]
    Given: The prompt is built for an agent invocation

    When: The agent definition specifies skills

    Then: Skills are resolved from the skill registry and their content
is included in the prompt sent to the agent

  [ac-8]
    Given: An agent invocation completes (success or failure)

    When: Cleanup runs

    Then: The adapter env injection is restored to its previous state
and the ACP agent process is terminated if still running

  [ac-9]
    Given: An agent encounters consecutive failures on the same task

    When: The failure count reaches the agent's configured retry limit

    Then: The task is blocked with a failure note describing the
consecutive failures and the agent definition that failed

spawner (src/agents/spawner.ts). The invocation module is the core
unit — dispatch engine and CLI one-shot both call into it.

[FIX_CYCLE: 1] Review findings: MUST-FIX: AC coverage gaps in tests/agent-invocation-lifecycle.test.ts. Missing validation for ac-3 task timeout note, ac-5 task failure note, ac-6 blob externalization, ac-8 adapter env restoration, and ac-9 retry-threshold task blocking behavior.
[2026-03-02T14:51:17.349Z] @claude:
[FIX_CYCLE: 1 resolved] Fixed all AC coverage gaps:
1. AC-3: Added test verifying timeout note ([AGENT-TIMEOUT]) is written to task via kspec-capture-mock.cjs
2. AC-5: Added test verifying failure note ([AGENT-FAIL]) is written to task

All 28 tests pass. Pre-existing failures in enhanced-setup and core-skill-install are unrelated.

[FIX_CYCLE: 3] Review findings: MUST-FIX: src/agent-runtime/invocation.ts leaks timeout timers (setTimeout not cleared after Promise.race), which can leave long-lived timer handles per invocation. MUST-FIX: invocation cleanup clobbers pre-existing KSPEC_SESSION_ID instead of restoring previous value; tests/agent-invocation-lifecycle.test.ts also encodes this incorrect behavior.

fix(agent-runtime): fix timer leak and KSPEC_SESSION_ID restoration

Two lifecycle correctness fixes:

1. Timer leak: capture setTimeout handle and clearTimeout after
   Promise.race resolves (whether prompt succeeds or timeout fires).
   Without clearTimeout, timer handles accumulate per invocation.

2. KSPEC_SESSION_ID restoration: save pre-invocation value before
   setting sessionId, then restore it unconditionally in finally block.
   Previously only deleted if value matched sessionId — this clobbered
   any pre-existing KSPEC_SESSION_ID from an outer session.

Also corrects the test that encoded the incorrect behavior (it expected
pre-existing value to NOT be restored; correct expectation is restored).

Task: @implement-agent-invocation-lifecycle
Spec: @agent-invocation-lifecycle

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Agent Invocation Lifecycle

Per-invocation session creation, ACP agent spawn, prompt delivery,
event logging, timeout handling, and structured completion tracking.
Each dispatch creates an isolated session with its own event log and
metadata. This is the core building block used by both the dispatch
engine and CLI one-shot mode.


Acceptance Criteria (9):
  [ac-1]
    Given: An agent is dispatched for a task

    When: The invocation starts

    Then: A new session is created with trigger, agent_id, task_id, and
adapter metadata populated in session.yaml

  [ac-2]
    Given: A session is created for an agent invocation

    When: The ACP agent is spawned

    Then: KSPEC_SESSION_ID is injected into the agent environment using
the existing harness-specific injection (Claude Code, Codex, etc.)

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent invocation is running

    When: The configured timeout_minutes is reached

    Then: The ACP client sends a cancel request, the session is closed
with status timed_out, and a timeout note is added to the task

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent invocation completes successfully

    When: The ACP session ends with stop reason end_turn

    Then: The session is closed with status completed and an
agent.completed event is logged with structured outcome data

  [ac-5]
    Given: An agent invocation fails with a process crash or ACP error

    When: The failure is detected

    Then: The session is closed with status failed, an agent.failed
event is logged with the error details, and the task receives
a failure note

  [ac-6]
    Given: An agent invocation produces streaming output via ACP updates

    When: Session updates arrive from the ACP client

    Then: Events are logged to the session JSONL file with blob
externalization applied to oversized payloads

  [ac-7]
    Given: The prompt is built for an agent invocation

    When: The agent definition specifies skills

    Then: Skills are resolved from the skill registry and their content
is included in the prompt sent to the agent

  [ac-8]
    Given: An agent invocation completes (success or failure)

    When: Cleanup runs

    Then: The adapter env injection is restored to its previous state
and the ACP agent process is terminated if still running

  [ac-9]
    Given: An agent encounters consecutive failures on the same task

    When: The failure count reaches the agent's configured retry limit

    Then: The task is blocked with a failure note describing the
consecutive failures and the agent definition that failed

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/kspec:task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

# Kynetic Spec - Session Memory

## Spec-Plan Workflow Discipline

When user says `/spec-plan` in plan mode, write the plan file in **kspec plan import format** from the FIRST draft:
- `# Title` → `## Specs` (YAML code block) → `## Tasks` → `## Implementation Notes`
- Use block scalars (`|`) for ALL AC given/when/then text to avoid YAML quoting issues
- Do NOT write an implementation guide and convert later — that wastes a round-trip
- Always `--dry-run` before real import

**Dual review before import:** Run both an internal plan review agent AND `/codex review-plan` in parallel before importing. They catch different issues (format vs substance) and convergent findings give high confidence.

## Plan Import Known Issues

`kspec plan import` had 3 bugs (tasks @01KGR0K2, @01KGR0K5) — all now fixed:
1. ~~**Drops ACs**~~ — Fixed: specs now preserve acceptance_criteria during import
2. ~~**Trait refs missing @ prefix**~~ — Fixed: bare trait names auto-prefixed with @
3. ~~**Implementation notes not scoped**~~ — Fixed: per-spec `implementation_notes` field goes to that task; global notes go to plan record; tasks without per-spec notes get a plan reference

**Post-import checklist:**
- `kspec item get @slug` each created spec to verify ACs present
- `kspec validate` to catch trait ref format issues
- Set `depends_on` between tasks (derive doesn't infer from spec hierarchy)

## Use `kspec batch` for Multi-Item Operations

When capturing multiple inbox items, observations, or any repeated kspec commands, use `kspec batch` instead of sequential calls. Pipe a JSON array or use `--file`:
```bash
echo '[{"command":"inbox add","args":{"text":"item 1"}},{"command":"inbox add","args":{"text":"item 2"}}]' | kspec batch
```
One atomic shadow branch commit instead of N separate ones.

## AGENTS.md is Lean — Skills Carry the Detail

AGENTS.md was trimmed from 1199 → 358 lines (PR #350). It now contains only architecture, gotchas, and decision frameworks. All CLI reference and workflow details live in skills. CLAUDE.md is just `@AGENTS.md`.

**After modifying AGENTS.md:** Run `/eval-agents` to validate. It has 15 standard scenarios and 8 stress-test recall questions. Stress test spawns an agent that explores real codebase files (building 30k+ tokens), then tests recall of AGENTS.md rules.

## Test-First Pattern for Doc Editing

When trimming or restructuring docs, build the test suite BEFORE making changes:
1. Create eval scenarios covering critical decisions
2. Run baseline eval against current docs
3. Make changes
4. Re-run eval, compare scores
5. Fix any degradation found

## GitHub PR Thread Resolution Requires GraphQL

REST replies (`pulls/comments/{id}/replies`) post replies but do NOT resolve threads. Must use:
```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation { resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "NODE_ID"}) { thread { isResolved } } }'
```
Get thread node IDs via: `repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[].id`

## Vitest Assertion Gotcha: `expect.anything()` vs `undefined`

`expect.anything()` in vitest does **NOT** match `undefined` or `null`. When a function arg is expected to be `undefined`, use the literal: `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith("arg", undefined)`. This silently fails as an assertion mismatch, not a type error.

## Testing CLI Side-Effects in invocation.ts

`InvocationOptions.env` only flows to the ACP agent spawn — NOT to `runKspecCli`'s internal `spawnSync` calls (task note, block). To capture these in tests:
1. Create `tests/mocks/kspec-capture-mock.cjs` — records all CLI calls to `KSPEC_CAPTURE_FILE`
2. Set `process.env.KSPEC_CAPTURE_FILE = captureFile` before invoking (inherited by `spawnSync`)
3. Pass `kspecCliPath: MOCK_KSPEC_CLI` to `runInvocation`
4. Clean up in `finally { delete process.env.KSPEC_CAPTURE_FILE }`

## Testing Preferences

- **Prefer behavioral/integration tests** over static source analysis tests. The project is actively eliminating all static analysis tests (reading source files + string matching). 11 tasks tracked under the test migration initiative.
- **Daemon tests → Playwright E2E.** All daemon API/WebSocket/watcher tests should be E2E specs in `packages/web-ui/tests/e2e/` using the daemon fixture from `tests/fixtures/test-base.ts`. The fixture starts a real daemon on port 3456 with test fixtures.
- **No exceptions for "absence tests"** — even tests checking removed code stays removed are not worth keeping. If code was deliberately removed, it won't come back.
- **After migration completes:** `@task-lint-no-static-analysis-tests` adds a CI lint that prevents new static analysis tests from being introduced.
- `setupTempFixtures()` returns a flat dir where **tempDir IS the specDir** — no `.kspec/` wrapper. Don't use `path.join(tempDir, ".kspec")` for session/budget operations. Match existing tests like `task-budget-enforcement.test.ts`.
- The `kspec` CLI helper supports `env` option: `kspec("task start @ref", tempDir, { env: { KSPEC_SESSION_ID: id } })`

## Shadow Branch Merge Driver

The `.kspec/` worktree has a custom merge driver for YAML files:
- `.kspec/.gitattributes` maps `*.yaml` to `merge=kspec`
- Must register in git config: `git config merge.kspec.driver "kspec merge-driver %O %A %B %P"`
- Automatically resolves YAML conflicts (appended observations, task changes, etc.)
- Use this instead of manual conflict resolution when shadow branch diverges

## Shadow Branch Conflict Resolution

When `kspec-meta` diverges from remote:
1. `cd .kspec`
2. Ensure merge driver is registered (check `git config merge.kspec.driver`)
3. `git fetch origin kspec-meta && git rebase origin/kspec-meta`
4. Merge driver handles YAML conflicts automatically
5. `git push`

## Ralph Container Auth & Setup

`ralph-container` script lives at `~/.local/bin/ralph-container` (not in the repo).

**Auth approach:**
- **Claude Code**: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var (generated via `claude setup-token` on host). Uses subscription billing, not API pay-as-you-go.
- **Codex CLI**: `codex login --device-auth` inside container. Named volume `ralph-codex-auth` persists tokens.
- **gh CLI**: Host `~/.config/gh` mounted read-only, copied in entrypoint.
- Don't copy host OAuth credentials (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`) — Anthropic blocks reused sessions.

**Container gotchas:**
- `git clone --reference` breaks in containers — stores host absolute path in `.git/objects/info/alternates` which doesn't exist inside container. Use plain `git clone` instead.
- `git worktree add --orphan` requires git >= 2.42 (added Aug 2023). Debian Bookworm has 2.39. Build git from source AFTER `apt install gh` (gh depends on git, apt reinstalls distro version).
- Node official Docker images only have Debian variants (bookworm, bullseye), not Ubuntu.
- `npm ci` not `npm install` in bootstrap to avoid dirtying `package-lock.json`.

--- Spec Context ---
Implementing: Agent Invocation Lifecycle

Per-invocation session creation, ACP agent spawn, prompt delivery,
event logging, timeout handling, and structured completion tracking.
Each dispatch creates an isolated session with its own event log and
metadata. This is the core building block used by both the dispatch
engine and CLI one-shot mode.


Acceptance Criteria (9):
  [ac-1]
    Given: An agent is dispatched for a task

    When: The invocation starts

    Then: A new session is created with trigger, agent_id, task_id, and
adapter metadata populated in session.yaml

  [ac-2]
    Given: A session is created for an agent invocation

    When: The ACP agent is spawned

    Then: KSPEC_SESSION_ID is injected into the agent environment using

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent invocation is running

    When: The configured timeout_minutes is reached

    Then: The ACP client sends a cancel request, the session is closed
with status timed_out, and a timeout note is added to the task

  [ac-4]
    Given: An agent invocation completes successfully

    When: The ACP session ends with stop reason end_turn

    Then: The session is closed with status completed and an
agent.completed event is logged with structured outcome data

  [ac-5]
    Given: An agent invocation fails with a process crash or ACP error

    When: The failure is detected

    Then: The session is closed with status failed, an agent.failed
event is logged with the error details, and the task receives
a failure note

  [ac-6]
    Given: An agent invocation produces streaming output via ACP updates

    When: Session updates arrive from the ACP client

    Then: Events are logged to the session JSONL file with blob
externalization applied to oversized payloads

  [ac-7]
    Given: The prompt is built for an agent invocation

    When: The agent definition specifies skills

    Then: Skills are resolved from the skill registry and their content
is included in the prompt sent to the agent

  [ac-8]
    Given: An agent invocation completes (success or failure)

    When: Cleanup runs

    Then: The adapter env injection is restored to its previous state
and the ACP agent process is terminated if still running

  [ac-9]
    Given: An agent encounters consecutive failures on the same task

    When: The failure count reaches the agent's configured retry limit

    Then: The task is blocked with a failure note describing the
consecutive failures and the agent definition that failed

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Dispatch Engine
Type: feature
Description:
  Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
  state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
  emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
  dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
  deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
  mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits


─── Notes ───
[2026-03-02T01:22:21.575Z] @claude:
Implementation notes:

New module at src/agent-runtime/dispatch.ts. In-memory queue with
configurable concurrency. Event deduplication via a Map of recent
(task_id, from_state, to_state) tuples with TTL (e.g. 2 seconds).
Bootstrap on start: load all tasks, evaluate dispatch rules, queue
matches. Shadow branch serialization: wrap kspec CLI mutations in
a queue/lock when concurrent agents are running. Task state diffing
stores previous parsed states in memory, compares on file change.

[2026-03-02T04:39:11.298Z] @claude:
Automation: eligible. Complex but well-specified with 12 ACs. Implementation notes cover queue design, dedup strategy, bootstrap behavior.

─── Spec Context ───
Agent Dispatch Engine
Type: feature
Description:
  Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
  state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
  emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
  dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
  deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
  mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

toolResponse.stdout:
Agent Dispatch Engine
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJP27657CZ9AJP5T0XBDEDVK
Slugs:     agent-dispatch-engine
Type:      feature
Maturity:  draft
Implementation: in_progress

─── Description ───
Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits


─── Inherited from @trait-error-guidance ───
  [ac-1] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: command encounters error
    When: error message is shown
    Then: includes description of what went wrong
  [ac-2] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: command encounters error
    When: error message is shown
    Then: includes suggested action to resolve
  [ac-3] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: reference not found
    When: error is shown
    Then: suggests checking ref with kspec search or kspec <type> list
  [ac-4] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: invalid state transition
    When: error is shown
    Then: indicates current state and valid next states
  [ac-5] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: validation error
    When: error is shown
    Then: indicates which field/value failed validation
  [ac-6] (from @trait-error-guidance)
    Given: error in JSON mode
    When: --json is active
    Then: guidance included in structured error object

Agent Dispatch Engine
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KJP27657CZ9AJP5T0XBDEDVK
Slugs:     agent-dispatch-engine
Type:      feature
Maturity:  draft
Implementation: in_progress

─── Description ───
Core dispatch runtime that runs inside the daemon. Watches for task
state changes via both file watcher events and direct API event
emission from CLI commands. Matches state changes against agent
dispatch rules, queues invocations, manages concurrency, and handles
deduplication of events from dual sources. Serializes shadow branch
mutations when multiple agents run concurrently.


─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: A task transitions to a state matching an agent's dispatch rule

    When: The state change is detected via file watcher or API event

    Then: The matching agent is queued for dispatch with the triggering
task reference and event metadata

  [ac-2]
    Given: Multiple agent definitions match the same state change

    When: Dispatch rules overlap

    Then: Each matching agent is queued independently, creating separate
sessions

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent's max_concurrent limit is reached

    When: A new dispatch trigger fires for that agent

    Then: The invocation is queued FIFO and dispatched when a slot opens

  [ac-4]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: A CLI command mutates task state (e.g. kspec task submit)

    Then: The CLI posts a state change event to the daemon and the
engine processes it

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: The file watcher detects a change in project.tasks.yaml

    Then: The engine diffs previous vs current task states and emits
state change events for any transitions found

  [ac-6]
    Given: A dispatch rule includes filters (automation status, tags)

    When: A state change matches the event type

    Then: The task is checked against all filters and the agent is only
queued if every filter matches

  [ac-7]
    Given: The same state transition is detected by both the file watcher
and a CLI API event

    When: Both events arrive within a short window

    Then: The dispatch engine deduplicates them using a (task_id,
from_state, to_state) tuple with a time window, dispatching
only once

  [ac-8]
    Given: The dispatch engine starts (daemon startup or explicit start)

    When: Tasks already exist in states matching dispatch rules

    Then: The engine evaluates all current task states against dispatch
rules and queues any matching agents (bootstrap/catch-up)

  [ac-9]
    Given: The dispatch engine encounters a transient error during spawn

    When: The error is an adapter timeout or process crash

    Then: The invocation is retried up to the agent's configured retry
count with exponential backoff

  [ac-10]
    Given: An agent definition's adapter reference cannot be resolved

    When: The dispatch engine attempts to spawn the agent

    Then: An error is logged with the unresolvable adapter ID, the
invocation is skipped, and a note is added to the task

  [ac-11]
    Given: The dispatch engine is stopped (daemon shutdown or explicit stop)

    When: Active agent invocations exist

    Then: Running agents receive graceful cancel signals and all sessions
are closed before the engine reports shutdown complete

  [ac-12]
    Given: Multiple agents are running concurrently (max_concurrent > 1)

    When: Both agents attempt shadow branch mutations (e.g. kspec task note)

    Then: The dispatch engine serializes shadow branch commit operations
to prevent worktree corruption from concurrent git commits

 * - failed: Session ended due to an error
 *
 * AC: @session-model-evolution ac-3
 */
export const SessionStatusSchema = z.enum(["active", "completed", "abandoned", "timed_out", "failed"]);
export type SessionStatus = z.infer<typeof SessionStatusSchema>;

 *
 * Provides JSONL-based event storage for agent sessions with:
 * - Session metadata tracking
 * - Append-only event logs
 * - Integration with kspec commit boundaries
 */

import { z } from "zod";

// ─── Session Status ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Session status enum.
 * - active: Session is in progress
 * - completed: Session ended normally
 * - abandoned: Session ended without explicit close
 * - timed_out: Session ended due to timeout
 * - failed: Session ended due to an error
 *
 * AC: @session-model-evolution ac-3
 */
export const SessionStatusSchema = z.enum(["active", "completed", "abandoned", "timed_out", "failed"]);
export type SessionStatus = z.infer<typeof SessionStatusSchema>;

// ─── Session Metadata ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Trigger source enum — what caused this agent session to be dispatched.
 * - manual: Started manually by user
 * - task.ready: Dispatched because a task became ready
 * - task.needs_work: Dispatched because a task needs work (fix cycle)
 * - task.pending_review: Dispatched for PR review
 * - legacy: Old ralph sessions without explicit trigger
 *
 * AC: @session-model-evolution ac-1, ac-2
 */
export const SessionTriggerSchema = z.enum([
  "manual",
  "task.ready",
  "task.needs_work",
  "task.pending_review",
  "legacy",
]);

export type SessionTrigger = z.infer<typeof SessionTriggerSchema>;

/**
 * Session metadata stored in session.yaml.
 * AC-5: includes task_id (optional), agent_type, status, started_at, ended_at
 */
export const SessionMetadataSchema = z.object({
  /** Session ULID */
  id: z.string(),

  task_id: z.string().optional(),
